artboards.title: 4 · A pet, as a follower sees it

annotations.text:
CRU-094 — the follower's path.
A follow is on a HOUSEHOLD, never on a pet.
Every household is private, so the link lands on a request, not on content.
Artboard 2 is the same route after the accept: the button reports state, it does not repeat the offer.

The boundary is posts and pet profiles.
Never feeds, never schedules, never reminders, never the Care Card. That is the RLS line and it is expensive to move.

Artboard 4 is its own route. The Member's pet screen is built on the ACTIVE household, whose timezone never arrives for a household you are not in — it would sit on its skeleton forever.

It carries no note about what is missing. A follower never expected feeds, so naming their absence only draws a line they could not see. The screen is simply short.

The Owner's path.
Only an Owner accepts or removes — the same gate as an Invite, and enforced by an RPC rather than by a write policy.
A Contributor helps with care. A Contributor does not decide who watches.

The two ways a follow ends are different events.
An unfollow is the follower's own, and repeatable. A removal by the Owner blocks the next request — one status column carries pending, accepted and removed.

Artboard 10 is a copy fix, not a new screen: Home tells a person with no household to create or join one, which is now only half of what they can do.
